common_confusions: BC-MIS-01017 (an average over an interval read as the rate at a point inside it)
BC-SKL-01003 (instantaneous rate, which requires the limiting step this skill does not take)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-01012 (average rates over shrinking intervals, where the quotient must be formed repeatedly and its structure is visible)
adaptive.mastered_if: The quotient of f(b) minus f(a) by b minus a is formed and evaluated for the interval the question names, from a formula and from a table of values, and the reported number carries the units of the quantity divided by the units of the input; the difference is never handed in as the rate (BC-ERR-01029 absent) and the interval endpoints match the rows the question specifies.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The correct pair of values is selected and subtracted but the division by b minus a is missing, which is BC-ERR-01029, or the quotient is set up correctly and the arithmetic in the division is wrong, which the 2014 Q4 commentary records as a computation loss inside a correct setup.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The values placed in the numerator come from the wrong input, or f and f prime are interchanged when reading the table, which is a function notation gap at BC-PRQ-06005 rather than a difficulty with the average rate.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-01017 (an average rate describes a whole interval, not one instant) for the conceptual failure; BC-PRQ-06005 (pulling f(b) and f(a) from the correct rows) for the procedural failure

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given f and an interval from a to b, compute the quotient of f(b) minus f(a) by b minus a.
skills.description_plain: Divide the change in the function by the change in the input over an interval.
skills.name: Compute an average rate of change over an interval

common_confusions: BC-MIS-01017 (an average over an interval treated as a rate at a point, which hides why the zero length case fails)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-01012 (intervals are shrunk towards a point, so the zero length case is the endpoint of the sequence and must be described rather than computed)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response states that the difference quotient divides by b minus a, that a single point gives b equal to a and therefore a zero denominator, and that no average rate is defined there, with the zero denominator named as the reason rather than a claim that the function stops existing.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The response says an average rate needs an interval but never names the zero denominator as the mechanism, so the explanation restates the conclusion instead of exhibiting the quotient that breaks down.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The response cannot write the quotient of f(b) minus f(a) by b minus a at all before discussing degeneracy, which is a function notation gap at BC-PRQ-06005.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-01017 (an average rate is an interval quantity) for the conceptual failure; BC-PRQ-06005 (writing the difference quotient in function notation) for the procedural failure

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: State that the difference quotient divides by the change in the independent variable, so a single point gives a zero denominator and no average rate.
skills.description_plain: Say why the quotient breaks down when the interval has zero length.
skills.name: Explain why an average rate of change is undefined at a single point

common_confusions: BC-MIS-01017 (an average rate over an interval taken to be the rate at a point in it)
BC-SKL-01001 (the average rate, which needs no limit)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-01012 (the task separates computing the averages from stating what they approach, so the limiting description is scored on its own)
adaptive.mastered_if: The instantaneous rate at a is written as the limit of average rates of f over intervals containing a as the interval length tends to zero, with the limit symbol present and the interval length named as the quantity tending to zero, and an average over a fixed interval is reported as an approximation rather than as the exact rate (BC-ERR-01030 absent).
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: A sequence of average rates is described correctly but the response names the last computed average as the rate at the point, which is BC-ERR-01030, or the word limit appears with no quantity tending to zero attached to it.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The average rates themselves are wrong or reported as differences, which is a gap at BC-SKL-01001 rather than in the limiting description, and pulling values for the wrong input is a BC-PRQ-06005 gap.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-01017 (why shrinking the interval changes the object being measured) for the conceptual failure; BC-SKL-01001 (forming each average rate correctly) for the procedural failure

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Express the instantaneous rate of change of f at a as the limit of average rates of change of f over intervals containing a as the interval length tends to zero.
skills.description_plain: Say that the rate at an instant is what the average rates approach as the interval closes in.
skills.name: Describe an instantaneous rate as a limit of average rates

common_confusions: BC-MIS-01001 (the limit at c written as the value of f at c)
BC-SKL-01007 (one sided notation, where a side must be carried on the arrow)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-01013 (a limit fact given in one representation must be produced in analytic form, so only the notation is at stake)
adaptive.mastered_if: The statement is written with the limit symbol, the independent variable, the arrow to the target input, and the claimed value, in the order lim as x approaches c of f(x) equals R, with the variable of approach named and no value substituted in place of the arrow, and the same statement is produced from a verbal description and from a graph.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The claimed value and the target input are both correct but the notation omits the variable under the arrow or writes f(c) where the limit symbol belongs, so the statement asserts evaluation rather than approach.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The response cannot say which symbol is the input and which is the output of f, or evaluates f at the wrong argument, which is a function notation gap at BC-PRQ-06005.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-01001 (what the limit symbol claims, as distinct from evaluation) for the conceptual failure; BC-PRQ-06005 (reading and writing function notation) for the procedural failure

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a function, a target input, and a claimed value, write the statement using the limit symbol, the independent variable, the arrow to the target, and the claimed value.
skills.description_plain: Turn a described approach into the limit symbols.
skills.name: Write a limit statement in correct analytic notation
skills.notation: lim as x approaches c of f(x) equals R

common_confusions: BC-MIS-01003 (a limit taken as a value the function must eventually attain)
BC-MIS-01001 (the limit read as the function value at c)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-01013 (an analytic statement must be matched to a graph or a table, so a wrong reading shows up as the wrong match)
adaptive.mastered_if: A written limit statement is read back as the claim that f(x) can be made arbitrarily close to the stated value by taking x sufficiently close to c and not equal to c, with the exclusion of x equal to c stated, and the reading does not assert that f attains the value at c or anywhere else.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The sentence describes the function approaching the value but adds that it reaches it, or omits the clause excluding x equal to c, so the reading is consistent with BC-MIS-01003 while the direction of approach is right.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The response cannot identify f, the input variable, and the target input inside the statement, which is a notation reading gap at BC-PRQ-06005 rather than a difficulty with the meaning of a limit.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-01003 (approach without attainment, including at inputs where f is undefined) for the conceptual failure; BC-PRQ-06005 (identifying the parts of the statement) for the procedural failure

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Read a limit statement as the claim that f(x) can be made arbitrarily close to the stated value by taking x sufficiently close to the target and not equal to it.
skills.description_plain: Say in words what a written limit statement claims about the function values.
skills.name: Interpret a limit statement given in analytic notation

common_confusions: BC-MIS-01002 (one side treated as settling the two sided limit)
BC-SKL-01005 (the two sided statement, which carries no side marker)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-01013 (a one sided behaviour shown graphically must be produced in analytic form, which isolates the side marker)
adaptive.mastered_if: The left hand and right hand statements at c are written with the side carried on the arrow as c from the left and c from the right, each with its own claimed value, and the two statements are kept separate rather than combined into one two sided claim.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The two one sided values are correct but the side marker is attached to the function or to the value instead of to the target input, or only one of the two statements is written where both are requested.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The two sided statement itself cannot be written with the limit symbol and the arrow, which places the failure at BC-SKL-01005, and misreading which argument f is evaluated at is a BC-PRQ-06005 gap.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-01002 (why each side is a separate claim) for the conceptual failure; BC-SKL-01005 (limit notation before a side is added) for the procedural failure

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Write the left hand and right hand limit statements at a target input using the correct one sided arrow notation.
skills.description_plain: Use the left and right arrows to say which side the approach comes from.
skills.name: Write one sided limit notation
skills.notation: lim as x approaches c from the left; lim as x approaches c from the right

common_confusions: BC-MIS-01002 (one sided approach taken as sufficient for the two sided limit)
BC-MIS-01001 (the plotted value read as the limit)
BC-SKL-01010 (one sided limits, which are reported separately and are not compared)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-01001 (a graph with breaks, where two sided and one sided values and the function value are requested at named inputs)
adaptive.mastered_if: The target input is located on the horizontal axis, the heights approached from the left and from the right are read, and the two are compared before a value is reported, so a jump yields the verdict that the limit does not exist rather than the height on one side (BC-ERR-01002 absent) and a plotted point that sits away from the approached height is not reported as the limit (BC-ERR-01001 absent).
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: One side is read correctly and reported as the limit while the other side is never examined, which is BC-ERR-01002, or the closed point rather than the approached height is handed in, which is BC-ERR-01001.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The heights are read at an input other than the one named, which is a graph reading gap at BC-PRQ-06005 rather than a limit gap.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-01002 (both sides required before a two sided verdict) for the conceptual failure; BC-PRQ-06005 (locating the named input and reading the approached height) for the procedural failure

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a graph of f, estimate the limit at a target input by reading the output the graph approaches from the left and from the right.
skills.description_plain: Read the height the graph heads towards from both sides.
skills.name: Estimate a two sided limit from a graph

common_confusions: BC-MIS-01002 (one side treated as settling the limit)
BC-SKL-01009 (the two sided estimate, which requires comparing the two readings)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-01001 (requests one sided values at a break as separate answers, so each side is scored on its own)
adaptive.mastered_if: The height approached from the left and the height approached from the right are reported as two separate answers with the side attached to each, including at an input where the two differ and at an input where the graph has a closed point at neither height, and neither one is promoted to a two sided claim (BC-ERR-01002 absent).
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: Both one sided heights are read correctly but the response labels them with the wrong sides, or answers the one sided question with a single two sided statement, which is BC-ERR-01002.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The reading is taken at the wrong input or the vertical and horizontal axes are interchanged, which is a graph reading gap at BC-PRQ-06005.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-01002 (each side is a claim in its own right) for the conceptual failure; BC-PRQ-06005 (reading a graph at a named input) for the procedural failure

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a graph of f, report the left hand and right hand limits at a target input as separate values.
skills.description_plain: Read separately the height approached from the left and from the right.
skills.name: Estimate one sided limits from a graph

common_confusions: BC-MIS-01012 (unbounded behaviour assumed identical on both sides, or infinity read as a real value)
BC-SKL-01011 (nonexistence from differing finite one sided limits)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-01001 (asks for the limit or a statement of nonexistence at an input where the graph is unbounded, with a reason required)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response states that the values of f increase or decrease without bound near c and concludes that the limit at c does not exist as a real number, keeping the distinction between writing an infinite limit as a description of behaviour and asserting that a real limit exists (BC-ERR-01020 absent).
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The unbounded behaviour is described correctly but the statement that the limit equals infinity is then treated as an existence claim, which is BC-ERR-01020, so the behaviour is right and the existence verdict is not.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The sign of the quotient on each side of the zero of the denominator cannot be determined, so one two sided infinite statement is written where the sides carry opposite signs, which is a sign analysis gap at BC-PRQ-01009.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-01012 (the infinity symbol as a description of behaviour rather than a value) for the conceptual failure; BC-PRQ-01009 (sign of the quotient on each side) for the procedural failure

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a function whose values increase or decrease without bound near c, conclude that the limit at c does not exist as a real number.
skills.description_plain: Say the limit does not exist when the values grow without bound.
skills.name: Determine that a limit fails to exist because the function is unbounded

common_confusions: BC-MIS-01004 (a table taken to settle the behaviour of the function)
BC-SKL-01012 (nonexistence from unbounded values, which is a different mechanism)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-01001 (nonexistence must be stated with a reason, which separates oscillation from a jump or unbounded growth)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response identifies that the values swing between fixed bounds arbitrarily close to c without settling, and concludes that the limit does not exist, rather than naming one of the values in the oscillation as the limit (BC-ERR-01004 absent); the verdict survives a table whose spacing happens to show agreeing values.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The oscillation is described correctly but one of the visited values is then reported as the limit, which is BC-ERR-01004, or the verdict rests only on the tabulated rows rather than on the behaviour between them.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The trigonometric factor cannot be bounded between negative one and one, so the oscillation is treated as unbounded growth, which is a gap at BC-PRQ-01005 rather than a misreading of nonexistence.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-01004 (what happens between tabulated inputs) for the conceptual failure; BC-PRQ-01005 (bounds on sine and cosine) for the procedural failure

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a function that oscillates between fixed values arbitrarily close to c without approaching a single value, conclude that the limit at c does not exist.
skills.description_plain: Say the limit does not exist when the values keep swinging without settling.
skills.name: Determine that a limit fails to exist because the function oscillates

common_confusions: BC-MIS-01004 (a finite sample, whether tabulated or plotted, treated as settling the behaviour)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-01013 (the same limit claim is presented graphically and analytically, so a graph that disagrees with the expression exposes the scale argument)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response states that a graph drawn at a given window may omit behaviour near the target input, for instance oscillation compressed below the pixel scale, and concludes that a limit read from a graph is provisional rather than established, naming the window or scale as the reason.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The response says the graph could be misleading but gives no mechanism, so the claim restates caution without naming what a wider or narrower window would reveal.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The limit cannot be read from the graph at the named input in the first place, which is a reading gap at BC-PRQ-06005 rather than a claim about scale.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-01004 (what a finite representation does and does not establish) for the conceptual failure; BC-PRQ-06005 (reading a graph at a named input) for the procedural failure

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: State that a graphical representation at a given scale may omit behaviour near the target input, so a graphical estimate of a limit is provisional.
skills.description_plain: Say why a graph on one window can mislead about a limit.
skills.name: Explain how the scale of a graph can hide function behaviour

common_confusions: BC-MIS-01004 (tabulated agreement treated as proof)
BC-SKL-01017 (judging what the table settles, which is the separate explanation task)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-01002 (a table approaching a target from both sides, with a separate point when the limitation of the table must be explained)
adaptive.mastered_if: The rows approaching c from the left and from the right are identified separately, the value the outputs crowd towards is stated from both sides, and the number is reported as an estimate supported by the table rather than as an established limit (BC-ERR-01005 absent).
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The correct value is read from the table but the response asserts it as established because the tabulated outputs agree to several places, which is BC-ERR-01005, or only the rows on one side are used for a two sided estimate.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The outputs are taken from rows for the wrong input, or the input and output columns are interchanged, which is a notation and reading gap at BC-PRQ-06005.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-01004 (behaviour between tabulated inputs) for the conceptual failure; BC-PRQ-06005 (identifying which rows lie on each side of c) for the procedural failure

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a table of values of f at inputs approaching c from both sides, report the value the outputs approach as the estimate of the limit at c.
skills.description_plain: Read the value the outputs crowd towards as the inputs close in from both sides.
skills.name: Estimate a two sided limit from a table of values

common_confusions: BC-MIS-01002 (a one sided estimate promoted to a two sided claim)
BC-SKL-01015 (the two sided estimate, which uses rows from both sides)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-01002 (asks for a one sided estimate from a table whose rows straddle the target, so row selection is the scored behaviour)
adaptive.mastered_if: Only the rows on the requested side of c are used, the side is named in the answer, and the value the outputs approach on that side is reported, with rows from the other side visibly excluded from the estimate.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The value is right but rows from both sides are averaged or listed together, so the one sided character of the estimate is not carried into the work.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The rows cannot be sorted into those above and below c, which is a notation and table reading gap at BC-PRQ-06005.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-01002 (what a one sided claim asserts) for the conceptual failure; BC-PRQ-06005 (reading rows against the target input) for the procedural failure

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a table of values of f, estimate the left hand or right hand limit at c using only the tabulated inputs on the requested side of c.
skills.description_plain: Use only the rows on one side of the target input.
skills.name: Estimate a one sided limit from a table of values

common_confusions: BC-MIS-01004 (tabulated agreement read as proof)
BC-SKL-01015 (producing the estimate, which this skill judges rather than computes)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-01002 (carries a separate point for explaining what the table does and does not establish)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response states that a finite table supports an estimate and does not establish a limit, and identifies a table whose spacing leaves the behaviour between rows undetermined, for instance rows sampled where an oscillating function repeats, so neither the agreeing values are taken as proof (BC-ERR-01005 absent) nor a visited value of an oscillation reported as the limit (BC-ERR-01004 absent).
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The response reports the estimate correctly and adds that the table is only evidence, but cannot say what behaviour the spacing could hide, so the limitation is asserted rather than located.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The rows cannot be matched to inputs on either side of c, which is a reading gap at BC-PRQ-06005 rather than a judgement about evidence.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-01004 (what a finite sample of inputs can support) for the conceptual failure; BC-PRQ-06005 (reading the table against the target input) for the procedural failure

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: State that a finite table of values supports an estimate but does not establish a limit, and identify tables whose spacing leaves the behaviour near c undetermined.
skills.description_plain: Decide whether the tabulated values really settle or only appear to.
skills.name: Judge whether a table supports a limit value or is inconclusive

common_confusions: BC-MIS-01005 (limit theorems applied without their conditions, which matters once quotients and composites appear)
BC-SKL-01020 (the quotient theorem, which carries a denominator condition this one does not)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-01003 (supplies two limits and asks for a combination, so the theorem rather than any algebra is at stake)
adaptive.mastered_if: With the limits of f and g at c supplied, the limit of f plus g or f minus g is reported as the corresponding sum or difference of those limits, the two supplied values are recorded before combining, and the order of subtraction matches the order in the expression.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The theorem is applied to the right pair of limits but the subtraction runs the wrong way, so only the sign of the result is wrong, or the supplied limits are combined before being recorded, leaving no work to support the value.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The supplied limits are read against the wrong function or the wrong target input, which is a function notation gap at BC-PRQ-06005.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-01005 (which theorem carries which condition) for the conceptual failure; BC-PRQ-06005 (matching each supplied limit to its function) for the procedural failure

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given that the limits of f and g at c exist, evaluate the limit of f plus g or f minus g as the corresponding sum or difference of those limits.
skills.description_plain: Split the limit of a sum into the sum of the limits.
skills.name: Apply the sum and difference limit theorems

common_confusions: BC-MIS-01005 (theorems applied as unconditional formal rules)
BC-SKL-01018 (the sum and difference case)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-01003 (a product or constant multiple built from two supplied limits, which isolates this theorem from any rewriting)
adaptive.mastered_if: The limit of a product is reported as the product of the supplied limits and a constant factor is carried outside the limit unchanged, with both supplied values recorded and the constant multiple case handled without re-deriving the product rule for it.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The product of the two limits is formed correctly but a constant multiple is also multiplied into itself or dropped, so the structure of the theorem is right and one factor is mishandled.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The supplied limits are matched to the wrong functions or the wrong target, which is a notation gap at BC-PRQ-06005.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-01005 (the hypotheses each limit theorem needs) for the conceptual failure; BC-PRQ-06005 (reading the supplied limits) for the procedural failure

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given that the limits of f and g at c exist, evaluate the limit of a product as the product of the limits and the limit of a constant multiple as the constant times the limit.
skills.description_plain: Take the limit of each factor and multiply, and pull constants out.
skills.name: Apply the product and constant multiple limit theorems

common_confusions: BC-MIS-01005 (limit theorems treated as unconditional)
BC-SKL-01029 (classifying the form under substitution, which is what a zero denominator limit calls for next)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-01003 (a quotient built from supplied limits, where the denominator condition is expected in a justified response)
adaptive.mastered_if: Before dividing, the response states that the limit of the denominator is not zero and then reports the quotient of the two limits, and where the denominator limit is zero it states that the theorem does not apply rather than dividing anyway (BC-ERR-01006 absent).
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The quotient of the two supplied limits is formed correctly and the denominator condition is never written down, so the value stands but the justification naming the theorem is incomplete.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The supplied limits are attached to the wrong functions, which is a notation gap at BC-PRQ-06005, rather than an omission of the condition.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-01005 (why the quotient theorem carries a denominator condition) for the conceptual failure; BC-SKL-01029 (classifying the form when the denominator limit is zero) for the procedural failure

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Evaluate the limit of a quotient as the quotient of the limits, stating first that the limit of the denominator is not zero, and identify when the theorem does not apply.
skills.description_plain: Divide the limits, after checking that the bottom limit is not zero.
skills.name: Apply the quotient limit theorem and check the denominator condition

common_confusions: BC-MIS-01019 (continuity read off the shape of the formula rather than from its domain)
BC-SKL-01029 (classifying the form, which is what substitution at an excluded input calls for)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-01014 (several expressions are presented and the procedure must be selected, so substituting where it does not apply is visible)
adaptive.mastered_if: For a polynomial, rational, power, exponential, logarithmic, or trigonometric expression defined at c, the response substitutes c and reports the resulting number as the limit, and states or implies that substitution is legitimate because the expression is defined and continuous there rather than as a default move.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: Substitution is carried out correctly where it is legitimate but is also attempted at an input outside the domain, so the value is produced without the check that licenses it.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The inputs at which a radical, logarithm, or rational expression is undefined cannot be named, which is a domain gap at BC-PRQ-01008 and shows up as substitution at an excluded input.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-01019 (continuity as a property on a domain) for the conceptual failure; BC-PRQ-01008 (domains of rational, radical, logarithmic, and trigonometric expressions) for the procedural failure

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: For a polynomial, rational, power, exponential, logarithmic, or trigonometric expression defined at c, evaluate the limit at c by substituting c.
skills.description_plain: Put the target value into the expression when that is legitimate.
skills.name: Evaluate a limit by direct substitution where the function is continuous

common_confusions: BC-MIS-01005 (composite and quotient theorems applied without their conditions)
BC-SKL-01021 (direct substitution, which handles the composite only when both parts are defined at c)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-01003 (a composite built from supplied limits, which isolates the order of application)
adaptive.mastered_if: The limit of the inner function at c is taken first, the outer function is then applied to that value, and the response records that the outer function is continuous at the inner limit, so the composite is evaluated in the order outer of inner rather than the reverse (BC-ERR-01007 absent).
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The inner limit is found correctly and the outer function applied, but the continuity condition on the outer function is never mentioned, so the theorem is used without its hypothesis.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The composite notation is misread, so the response cannot say which function is inner and which is outer, which is a gap at BC-PRQ-06005 rather than an error in the theorem.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-01005 (the continuity condition on the outer function) for the conceptual failure; BC-PRQ-06005 (reading composite notation) for the procedural failure

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given the limit of the inner function at c and continuity of the outer function at that value, evaluate the limit of the composite as the outer function of the inner limit.
skills.description_plain: Take the limit of the inside first, then apply the outside function.
skills.name: Apply the limit theorem for composite functions

common_confusions: BC-MIS-01002 (one side taken as sufficient)
BC-SKL-01044 (the continuity test, which adds the comparison with the defined value)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-01006 (a piecewise rule at a named input, where the two branch evaluations are separately visible)
adaptive.mastered_if: At a branch boundary the left hand limit is evaluated from the branch that applies to the left and the right hand limit from the branch that applies to the right, the two are compared, and the two sided limit is reported only when they agree, with each substitution visibly taken into the branch whose condition covers that side (BC-ERR-01017 absent).
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: One of the two one sided limits is computed from the branch that does not apply on that side, which is BC-ERR-01017, so the comparison is carried out on a wrong value, or the two values agree and the response never states the two sided conclusion.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The branch conditions cannot be matched to inputs at all, so the boundary input is substituted into whichever expression is written first, which is a piecewise reading gap at BC-PRQ-01003.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-01002 (why both branches must be evaluated) for the conceptual failure; BC-PRQ-01003 (matching a branch condition to a side of the boundary) for the procedural failure

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: For a piecewise defined function, evaluate the left hand and right hand limits at a boundary from the relevant branch expressions and report the two sided limit when they agree.
skills.description_plain: Evaluate each branch at the boundary and compare.
skills.name: Determine a two sided limit by matching one sided limits of a piecewise rule

common_confusions: BC-MIS-01006 (zero over zero read as a verdict)
BC-SKL-01024 (the factoring route, which applies when no radical is present)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-01004 (an indeterminate quotient whose rewriting step is scored separately from the value)
adaptive.mastered_if: A quotient containing a radical difference that is indeterminate at c is multiplied above and below by the conjugate, the difference of squares is formed and simplified, the common factor is divided out, and the remaining expression is evaluated at c, with the form established by the two separate limits before the rewriting begins.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The conjugate is chosen correctly but the product in the numerator is expanded wrongly, or the conjugate is multiplied into only one of numerator and denominator, so the rewritten expression is no longer equivalent to the original.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The radical difference is left in place and the limit reported as nonexistent, which is a rationalising gap at BC-PRQ-01002; failing to see that the form demands a rewriting at all is a BC-SKL-01028 gap.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-01006 (an indeterminate form as a signal, not a value) for the conceptual failure; BC-PRQ-01002 (rationalising with a conjugate) for the procedural failure

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a quotient involving a sum or difference with a radical that is indeterminate at c, multiply numerator and denominator by the conjugate, simplify, and evaluate.
skills.description_plain: Clear the radical with the conjugate, then cancel and substitute.
skills.name: Evaluate an indeterminate limit by multiplying by a conjugate

common_confusions: BC-MIS-01007 (cancellation as a syntactic move on matching symbols)
BC-SKL-01024 (the factoring route, which applies once the fraction is cleared)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-01004 (the rewriting step carries its own credit, so clearing the inner fractions is visible)
adaptive.mastered_if: A quotient whose numerator or denominator contains fractions is multiplied through by the common denominator of the inner fractions, the compound expression is reduced to a single quotient, the common factor is divided out, and the limit is evaluated, with no summand cancelled in place of a factor (BC-ERR-01010 absent).
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The complex fraction is cleared correctly but a term common to numerator and denominator is then cancelled as though it were a factor, which is BC-ERR-01010, so the rewriting is undone by the final move.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The difference of two fractions in the numerator cannot be combined over a common denominator, which is a gap at BC-PRQ-01007; not recognising that the zero over zero form calls for a rewriting is a BC-SKL-01028 gap.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-01007 (equivalence of the rewritten expression) for the conceptual failure; BC-PRQ-01007 (simplifying a complex fraction) for the procedural failure

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a quotient whose numerator or denominator contains fractions, multiply through by a common denominator, simplify, and evaluate the limit.
skills.description_plain: Clear the nested fractions first, then cancel and substitute.
skills.name: Evaluate an indeterminate limit by simplifying a complex fraction

common_confusions: BC-MIS-01006 (the indeterminate form treated as an answer)
BC-SKL-01024 (the factoring route, which does not resolve a trigonometric indeterminacy)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-01004 (a quotient that gives zero over zero and must be rewritten into an equivalent form before evaluation)
adaptive.mastered_if: A trigonometric quotient that is indeterminate at c is rewritten with a Pythagorean, double angle, or reciprocal identity into an expression whose limit can be read off, the identity used is visible in the work, and the value follows from the rewritten form rather than from substitution into the original.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: An identity is applied correctly but the resulting expression is not simplified far enough to remove the indeterminacy, so the response stops at a second zero over zero form.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: Exact values of sine and cosine at the target angle are unavailable, or the oscillating factor cannot be bounded, which is a gap at BC-PRQ-01005; not seeing that the form requires rewriting is a BC-SKL-01028 gap.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-01006 (an indeterminate form as a signal to rewrite) for the conceptual failure; BC-PRQ-01005 (exact trigonometric values and bounds) for the procedural failure

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a trigonometric quotient that is indeterminate at c, apply an identity or an alternate form to produce an equivalent expression whose limit can be read off.
skills.description_plain: Use an identity to turn the expression into one that can be evaluated.
skills.name: Evaluate an indeterminate limit by rewriting with trigonometric identities

common_confusions: BC-MIS-01006 (an indeterminate form read as a value)
BC-SKL-01030 (choosing the procedure, which follows the classification)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-01014 (the classification and the resulting value carry separate credit, so a correct value from a wrong label is visible)
adaptive.mastered_if: The target input is substituted and the result named as one of a determinate value, the indeterminate form zero over zero, or a nonzero number over zero, with the nonzero over zero case distinguished from the indeterminate case and neither reported as an answer (BC-ERR-01008 and BC-ERR-01009 absent) and no quotient theorem applied over a zero denominator limit (BC-ERR-01006 absent).
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: Substitution is carried out and the resulting form written down, but zero over zero and nonzero over zero are given the same label, so the classification does not distinguish a rewriting case from an unbounded case.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: Substitution into a defined expression is itself mishandled, which is a BC-SKL-01021 gap, and inability to factor once the form is named is a BC-PRQ-01001 gap rather than a classification failure.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-01006 (what each form does and does not determine) for the conceptual failure; BC-SKL-01021 (substituting correctly before classifying) for the procedural failure

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Substitute the target input into the expression and classify the result as a determinate value, the indeterminate form zero over zero, or a nonzero number over zero.
skills.description_plain: Substitute first and name what comes out: a value, zero over zero, or an unbounded quotient.
skills.name: Classify a limit expression by its form under substitution

common_confusions: BC-MIS-01006 (an indeterminate form read as a verdict rather than as a routing signal)
BC-SKL-01031 (recognising that substitution already settles the limit)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-01014 (several expressions are presented and the procedure for each must be identified, which is exactly this selection)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response names substitution, algebraic rewriting, one sided analysis, the squeeze theorem, or end behaviour comparison as the procedure the expression calls for and gives the reason from the form obtained under substitution, so a zero over zero quotient is routed to rewriting rather than declared nonexistent (BC-ERR-01009 absent).
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: A workable procedure is named but the reason is the surface appearance of the expression rather than the form under substitution, so the selection happens to fit this expression without a rule behind it.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The form under substitution is labelled wrongly in the first place, which is a BC-SKL-01029 gap, or the chosen rewriting cannot be carried out because the factorisation is unavailable, which is BC-PRQ-01001.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-01006 (what the form signals) for the conceptual failure; BC-SKL-01029 (classifying the form before selecting) for the procedural failure

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a limit expression, select substitution, algebraic rewriting, one sided analysis, the squeeze theorem, or end behaviour comparison as the procedure that resolves it, and name the reason.
skills.description_plain: Pick the method that suits the form the expression takes.
skills.name: Select an appropriate procedure for a given limit expression

common_confusions: BC-MIS-01019 (continuity attributed to the formula rather than to its domain)
BC-SKL-01030 (selecting a procedure, where substitution is one of the options)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-01014 (a mixed set where some expressions need no rewriting, so unnecessary machinery is visible)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response identifies that the expression is defined and continuous at c, reports the substituted value as the limit, and stops, with no factoring, conjugate, or identity applied to an expression that needs none.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The substituted value is correct but the response then rewrites the expression anyway, so the stopping rule is absent while the value survives.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: An input outside the domain of a radical, logarithm, or rational expression is treated as a point of continuity, which is a domain gap at BC-PRQ-01008.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-01019 (continuity on a domain) for the conceptual failure; BC-PRQ-01008 (locating the excluded inputs) for the procedural failure

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Identify expressions defined and continuous at the target input, for which substitution gives the limit and no further manipulation is warranted.
skills.description_plain: Stop rewriting when the direct value is legitimate.
skills.name: Recognise when substitution already settles the limit

common_confusions: BC-MIS-01008 (the theorem read as a rule for evaluating the bounds at c)
BC-MIS-01010 (naming the theorem treated as the argument)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-01005 (the bounding inequality, the limits of the bounds, and the conclusion each carry credit, so a missing hypothesis is visible)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response states both hypotheses, that the bounding inequality holds for all inputs near c except possibly at c itself, and that the two bounding functions have the same limit at c, and says that the inequality need not hold at c.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The bounding inequality is stated but the requirement that the two bounds share a limit is left out, or the inequality is required to hold at c as well, so the hypotheses are over or under stated.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The neighbourhood is written as a closed interval containing c where an open interval excluding c is meant, which is an interval notation gap at BC-PRQ-01010.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-01008 (the bounds as functions whose limits must agree) for the conceptual failure; BC-PRQ-01010 (interval and inequality notation) for the procedural failure

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: State that the bounding inequality must hold for all inputs near the target except possibly at the target, and that the two bounding functions must have the same limit there.
skills.description_plain: Name what must hold before the theorem may be used.
skills.name: State the hypotheses of the squeeze theorem

common_confusions: BC-MIS-01008 (the inequality handled as an equation)
BC-SKL-01035 (the full application, which uses this inequality)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-01005 (establishing the bounding inequality carries its own credit, separate from the conclusion)
adaptive.mastered_if: The oscillating factor is bounded between fixed values, the inequality is multiplied by the vanishing factor with the direction reversed wherever that factor is negative, and the resulting inequality is stated for inputs near c, so no sign changing multiplication passes without reversal (BC-ERR-01012 absent).
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The bound on the oscillating factor is correct and the multiplication is carried out, but the inequality direction is kept on the side where the vanishing factor is negative, which is BC-ERR-01012.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The trigonometric factor cannot be bounded between negative one and one and is treated as unbounded, which is a gap at BC-PRQ-01005 rather than an inequality handling error.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-01008 (what the bounding inequality asserts and where) for the conceptual failure; BC-PRQ-01005 (bounds on sine and cosine) for the procedural failure

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a candidate pair of bounding functions, establish the inequality for inputs near the target, typically from the bounds on a trigonometric factor.
skills.description_plain: Show the function really sits between the two bounds near the point.
skills.name: Verify the bounding inequality on an interval around the point

common_confusions: BC-MIS-01008 (the bounds evaluated at the target rather than taken as limits)
BC-SKL-01013 (oscillation as a reason for nonexistence, which is the case where no vanishing factor traps it)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-01005 (a function trapped between two bounds, with the inequality, the bound limits, and the conclusion each carrying credit)
adaptive.mastered_if: For a product of a vanishing factor and a bounded oscillating factor, the oscillating factor is bounded between negative one and one, the inequality is multiplied by the vanishing factor with the direction handled on each side (BC-ERR-01012 absent), both bounds are shown to tend to zero, and the limit of the product is concluded to be zero.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The bounding and the multiplication are correct but the conclusion is stated for the bounds only, without transferring the limit to the trapped product, so the last step of the theorem is missing.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The oscillating trigonometric factor cannot be bounded and is treated as growing without bound, which is a BC-PRQ-01005 gap, and a failure to reverse the inequality under a negative factor sits at BC-SKL-01033.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-01008 (what the theorem concludes and from what) for the conceptual failure; BC-SKL-01033 (multiplying the inequality correctly) for the procedural failure

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: For a product of a factor tending to zero and a bounded oscillating factor, bound the oscillating factor, multiply the inequality by the vanishing factor, and conclude the limit is zero.
skills.description_plain: Bound the oscillating part between negative one and one and multiply through.
skills.name: Apply the squeeze theorem to a bounded oscillating factor

common_confusions: BC-MIS-01018 (every statement containing an infinity symbol read as the same claim)
BC-SKL-01059 (horizontal asymptotes, one of the two statements being distinguished)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-01013 (one limit fact presented in one representation with the equivalent required in another, which is the conversion itself)
adaptive.mastered_if: A limit fact given as a graph, a table, or an expression is restated in neutral terms and each candidate presentation is tested against it, so a vertical asymptote statement is matched to unbounded behaviour near a finite input and an end behaviour statement to a horizontal asymptote, with the two never exchanged (BC-ERR-01033 absent).
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The behaviour is read correctly from the supplied representation but the candidate chosen carries the infinity symbol in the other position, so a statement about large inputs is matched to one about unbounded outputs.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The supplied representation is read at the wrong input, or the roles of f and its argument are interchanged, which is a notation gap at BC-PRQ-06005.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-01018 (where the infinity symbol sits and what each position claims) for the conceptual failure; BC-PRQ-06005 (reading the supplied representation) for the procedural failure

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a limit claim in one representation, identify the graph, table, or expression among alternatives that carries the same limit behaviour at the target input.
skills.description_plain: Check that the three presentations of one limit agree.
skills.name: Match a graph, a table, and an analytic expression of the same limit

common_confusions: BC-MIS-01018 (all infinity notation read as one claim)
BC-SKL-01006 (interpreting a finite two sided statement, which carries no infinity symbol)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-01013 (requires the verbal presentation of a limit supplied analytically, so the wording is the scored object)
adaptive.mastered_if: An analytic statement, including a one sided or infinite one, is converted into a sentence naming the input being approached, the side where one is specified, and what the outputs do, so unbounded growth near a finite input and settling towards a value for large inputs are described differently (BC-ERR-01033 absent).
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The sentence describes the correct behaviour but omits the side on a one sided statement, or describes outputs growing without bound as the input growing without bound, so the two roles of the infinity symbol are blurred in the wording.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The function, the variable, and the target cannot be identified inside the statement, which is a notation gap at BC-PRQ-06005.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-01018 (the two positions of the infinity symbol) for the conceptual failure; BC-PRQ-06005 (parsing the statement) for the procedural failure

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Convert an analytic limit statement, including a one sided or infinite statement, into a sentence describing the behaviour of the function near the target input.
skills.description_plain: Say in ordinary words what the symbols claim about the function near the point.
skills.name: Translate a limit statement into a verbal description of behaviour

common_confusions: BC-MIS-01001 (the limit drawn as the function value at the same input)
BC-SKL-01008 (distinguishing the limit from the value, which the sketch must embody)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-01013 (a limit claim must be produced in graphical form, so every stated condition is checkable against the drawing)
adaptive.mastered_if: A single curve is drawn satisfying every stated condition at once, with an open circle where the limit exists and the value differs or is undefined, a filled point at the stated value of f, and distinct one sided heights where a one sided condition demands them, and each condition can be pointed to on the sketch.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: Most conditions are met but the sketch places the filled point at the limit height where the conditions require it elsewhere, so the graph satisfies the limit conditions and contradicts the value condition.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: A piecewise description cannot be turned into branches with their conditions, so the sketch ignores which rule applies on which side, which is a gap at BC-PRQ-01003.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-01001 (the limit and the value as separate conditions) for the conceptual failure; BC-PRQ-01003 (reading a piecewise description) for the procedural failure

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given conditions on one sided limits, the two sided limit, and the function value at one or more inputs, produce a graph satisfying all of them simultaneously.
skills.description_plain: Draw a curve that meets every limit and value condition given.
skills.name: Sketch a graph consistent with stated limit and value conditions

common_confusions: BC-MIS-01011 (every input missing from the domain read as an asymptote)
BC-SKL-01041 (an infinite discontinuity, where the factor does not divide out)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-01007 (each break must be classified as removable, jump, or asymptotic, with a reason when justification is demanded)
adaptive.mastered_if: A break at c is named removable when the two sided limit at c exists while f(c) is undefined or differs from that limit, with both the limit and the status of f(c) stated, and the limit is not declared nonexistent merely because f has no value at c (BC-ERR-01003 absent).
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The limit is computed correctly and the break is called removable, but the response never compares the limit with f(c), so the classification rests on the existence of the limit alone.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The common factor that makes the limit exist is never divided out because the numerator and denominator are not factored, which is a gap at BC-PRQ-01001.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-01011 (what distinguishes a repaired point from an asymptote) for the conceptual failure; BC-PRQ-01001 (factoring and dividing out) for the procedural failure

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Identify a discontinuity at c as removable when the two sided limit at c exists while f(c) is undefined or differs from that limit.
skills.description_plain: Name a break removable when the limit exists but the value does not match it.
skills.name: Classify a removable discontinuity

common_confusions: BC-MIS-01002 (one side taken as settling the limit, which hides the jump)
BC-SKL-01039 (a removable break, where the two sides agree)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-01007 (several breaks of different kinds are presented, so a jump must be separated from a removable and an infinite break)
adaptive.mastered_if: A break at c is named a jump when both one sided limits exist as real numbers and differ, with the two values displayed, and the classification is not applied where one of the sides is unbounded or where the two sides agree.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: Both one sided limits are found and the verdict is a jump, but only one value is recorded, so the inequality that defines the classification is not exhibited.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: A boundary input is evaluated in the branch that does not apply on that side, which is BC-PRQ-01003, or an absolute value quotient is treated as having equal one sided limits, which is BC-PRQ-01006.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-01002 (both sides as separate claims) for the conceptual failure; BC-PRQ-01003 (evaluating the correct branch on each side) for the procedural failure

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Identify a discontinuity at c as a jump when both one sided limits at c exist as real numbers and are unequal.
skills.description_plain: Name a break a jump when both sides settle but at different heights.
skills.name: Classify a jump discontinuity

common_confusions: BC-MIS-01011 (every zero of the original denominator read as an asymptote)
BC-SKL-01039 (a removable break at a factor that divides out)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-01007 (classification of each break with a reason)
BC-QA-01009 (asymptote locations and the one sided behaviour stated in notation, which forces the sign work)
adaptive.mastered_if: A break at c is named as due to a vertical asymptote when at least one one sided limit there is infinite, with the unbounded side identified, and the classification is applied only after common factors have been divided out so that a cancelling factor is not reported as an asymptote (BC-ERR-01018 absent).
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The unbounded behaviour is identified correctly but the response reports the same infinite behaviour on both sides without checking the sign of the quotient on each, so the classification is right and the description of the sides is not.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The sign of the quotient just to the left and just to the right of the zero of the denominator cannot be determined, which is a gap at BC-PRQ-01009.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-01011 (simplify before reading unbounded behaviour) for the conceptual failure; BC-PRQ-01009 (sign analysis near a zero of the denominator) for the procedural failure

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Identify a discontinuity at c as due to a vertical asymptote when at least one one sided limit at c is infinite.
skills.description_plain: Name a break infinite when the values grow without bound on at least one side.
skills.name: Classify a discontinuity due to a vertical asymptote

common_confusions: BC-MIS-01019 (continuity read from the family of the formula rather than from its domain)
BC-SKL-01048 (determining continuity on intervals, which uses this list)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-01006 (a piecewise rule tested at a named input, where the candidate inputs must first be located)
adaptive.mastered_if: Every candidate input is listed, meaning each boundary of the partition and each input excluded from the branch expression that covers it, and the list is produced from the rule rather than from a graph, with branch conditions matched to sides correctly (BC-ERR-01017 absent).
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The partition boundaries are all listed but inputs where a branch expression is itself undefined, such as a zero of a denominator inside a branch, are omitted, so the search is limited to the seams of the rule.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: Branch conditions cannot be read, so an input is assigned to the wrong branch, which is BC-PRQ-01003, or the excluded inputs of a rational or radical branch cannot be found, which is BC-PRQ-01008.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-01019 (a break can sit inside a branch, not only at a seam) for the conceptual failure; BC-PRQ-01008 (domains of branch expressions) for the procedural failure

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a piecewise rule, locate every input at which the function may fail to be continuous, including boundaries of the partition and points excluded from a branch expression.
skills.description_plain: Check each branch boundary and each point excluded from a branch domain.
skills.name: Identify the discontinuities of a piecewise defined function from its rule

common_confusions: BC-MIS-01009 (one of the three conditions held as the whole definition)
BC-MIS-01001 (the limit read as the value, which collapses the third condition)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-01006 (the failing condition must be named, which requires the three to be held apart)
adaptive.mastered_if: All three conditions are stated, that f(c) exists, that the limit of f at c exists, and that the limit equals f(c), as separate requirements, and the response does not offer the existence of f(c) alone or agreement of the one sided limits alone as the definition (BC-ERR-01014 absent).
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: Two of the three conditions are stated and the third, usually the equality of the limit with the value, is folded into one of the others, so the definition is close but not separable into what can be checked.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The symbols f(c) and the limit of f at c cannot be told apart in writing, which is a function notation gap at BC-PRQ-06005.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-01009 (the three conditions as independent requirements) for the conceptual failure; BC-PRQ-06005 (writing f(c) and the limit distinctly) for the procedural failure

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: State that f is continuous at c provided f(c) exists, the limit of f at c exists, and the limit equals f(c).
skills.description_plain: Name the value, the limit, and their agreement.
skills.name: State the three conditions of continuity at a point

common_confusions: BC-MIS-01010 (restating the definition treated as justification)
BC-MIS-01009 (one condition held as the whole definition, so the wrong one is named)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-01006 (carries a justification point that requires naming the failed condition rather than restating the definition)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response names which of the three conditions fails and displays the values that show the failure, for instance the two unequal one sided limits or the limit alongside a different f(c), rather than citing the definition of continuity as the reason (BC-ERR-01016 absent).
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The verdict is correct and a condition is named, but no values are supplied to show the failure, so the reason remains a label rather than an argument.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The values themselves are wrong because the test was executed incorrectly, which is a BC-SKL-01044 gap, and reading f and its limit off the wrong input is BC-PRQ-06005.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-01010 (what makes a claim justified rather than asserted) for the conceptual failure; BC-SKL-01044 (producing the values the reason cites) for the procedural failure

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Support a claim that f is not continuous at c by naming which of the three conditions fails and giving the values that show the failure.
skills.description_plain: Point to the exact condition that breaks rather than restating the definition.
skills.name: Justify a continuity conclusion by naming the failed condition

common_confusions: BC-MIS-01019 (continuity read off the formula rather than the domain)
BC-SKL-01049 (open against closed interval continuity, which governs the endpoints)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-01015 (intervals and the reason naming the family and its domain carry separate credit)
adaptive.mastered_if: Every input at which the expression is undefined is located, the family of the expression is named as continuous on its domain, and the maximal intervals are written with the excluded inputs outside them and open brackets at those inputs (BC-ERR-01031 and BC-ERR-01032 absent).
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The excluded inputs are found correctly but an interval is written with a closed bracket at one of them, which is BC-ERR-01032, or one excluded input is swallowed inside a stated interval, which is BC-ERR-01031.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The zeros of a denominator, the sign condition of a radicand, or the domain of a logarithm cannot be produced, which is a gap at BC-PRQ-01008, and not knowing which families are continuous on their domains is a BC-SKL-01047 gap.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-01019 (continuity as a property on a domain) for the conceptual failure; BC-PRQ-01008 (finding the excluded inputs) for the procedural failure

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a rational, radical, logarithmic, or trigonometric expression, determine the inputs at which it is undefined and state the maximal intervals on which the function is continuous.
skills.description_plain: Exclude the inputs where the expression is undefined and report the rest as intervals.
skills.name: Determine intervals of continuity from the domain of an expression

common_confusions: BC-MIS-01019 (a formula in a continuous family read as continuous everywhere)
BC-SKL-01046 (writing the intervals, which this reason supports)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-01015 (a reason point requires naming the family and its domain, which is this statement)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response states that polynomial, rational, power, exponential, logarithmic, and trigonometric functions are continuous at every point of their domains, and uses that statement as the reason inside a continuity claim, with the qualification on the domain carried rather than dropped.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The families are named correctly but the reason is given as continuity everywhere, so the domain qualification is lost and the statement over claims for a rational or logarithmic expression.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The domain of the expression cannot be produced, so the qualification cannot be applied even when it is stated, which is a gap at BC-PRQ-01008.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-01019 (family membership together with the domain) for the conceptual failure; BC-PRQ-01008 (producing the domain) for the procedural failure

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: State that polynomial, rational, power, exponential, logarithmic, and trigonometric functions are continuous at every point of their domains, and use that to support a continuity claim.
skills.description_plain: Recall which standard families are continuous wherever they are defined.
skills.name: Name the function families continuous on their domains

common_confusions: BC-MIS-01019 (continuity inferred from the formulas without their domains)
BC-SKL-01044 (the point test, which this skill applies at each boundary)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-01015 (the intervals and the reason are scored separately on a function given by a rule)
adaptive.mastered_if: Each branch is confirmed continuous on the interior of its own piece from the family of its expression, each boundary is tested separately by comparing the one sided limits with the defined value, and the intervals of continuity are then assembled with no excluded input inside them (BC-ERR-01031 absent).
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The branches are handled correctly and the boundaries are not tested, so the answer reports continuity on the union of the pieces without settling whether the seams hold.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: An input is assigned to the wrong branch, which is BC-PRQ-01003, or the excluded inputs of a branch expression cannot be found, which is a BC-SKL-01046 gap.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-01019 (the domain governs the interval) for the conceptual failure; BC-SKL-01046 (assembling maximal intervals) for the procedural failure

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: For a piecewise defined function, confirm continuity on each branch from its expression and test each boundary separately, then state the intervals of continuity.
skills.description_plain: Check each branch on its own and then each boundary.
skills.name: Determine continuity of a piecewise function on an interval

common_confusions: BC-MIS-01011 (an input missing from the domain assumed to be an asymptote and so unrepairable)
BC-SKL-01053 (deciding whether the break can be removed, which precedes the repair)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-01008 (a piecewise rule whose unknown value at a boundary must be chosen so the function is continuous)
adaptive.mastered_if: The two sided limit at c is computed, f(c) is defined or redefined to equal that limit, and the response states that the extended function now satisfies the three conditions at c, with the repair applied only where the limit exists.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The limit is computed correctly but the new value is stated without saying that the redefined function is now continuous at c, so the repair is made and its effect is not claimed.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The common factor is never divided out so the limit is not available, which is a factoring gap at BC-PRQ-01001, and misclassifying the break as removable in the first place is a BC-SKL-01039 gap.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-01011 (which breaks can be repaired and why) for the conceptual failure; BC-PRQ-01001 (dividing out the common factor to get the limit) for the procedural failure

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a function with a removable discontinuity at c, define or redefine f(c) as the limit of f at c and state that the resulting function is continuous at c.
skills.description_plain: Set the value at the point equal to the limit there.
skills.name: Redefine a function value to remove a removable discontinuity

common_confusions: BC-MIS-01009 (continuity handled as one condition, so a boundary equation omits the value)
BC-SKL-01051 (the single parameter case)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-01008 (explicitly covers a rule with two unknown constants and two boundaries)
adaptive.mastered_if: One matching equation is formed at each of the two boundaries, each from the branch expressions that meet there, and the two equations are solved together as a system for the two constants, with both equations displayed and the solution checked against both boundaries.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: Both equations are formed correctly but only one is used, so one constant is determined and the other is left or guessed, or the system is set up and the algebra of solving it fails.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: A single boundary condition cannot be written with the defined value included, which is a BC-SKL-01051 gap, and assigning an input to the wrong branch is BC-PRQ-01003.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-01009 (each boundary imposes its own full condition) for the conceptual failure; BC-SKL-01051 (forming one matching equation) for the procedural failure

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a piecewise rule with two unknown constants and two boundaries, form the matching equation at each boundary and solve the resulting system.
skills.description_plain: Write one equation per boundary and solve the pair together.
skills.name: Solve for two parameters using continuity conditions at two boundaries

common_confusions: BC-MIS-01011 (any input outside the domain assumed to be an asymptote)
BC-SKL-01050 (carrying out the repair once it is known to be possible)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-01008 (a rule whose continuity must be arranged, where an irreparable break shows as an unsolvable matching equation)
adaptive.mastered_if: The two sided limit at the discontinuity is examined first, and the break is called removable only when that limit exists, so an input where f is undefined but both sides agree is reported as repairable and one where the sides differ or are unbounded is not (BC-ERR-01003 absent).
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The limit is examined and found to exist but the verdict rests on f being undefined at c rather than on the limit, so the right answer follows from the wrong test.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The one sided limits at a branch boundary are taken from the wrong branches, which is a gap at BC-PRQ-01003 rather than a failure of the criterion.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-01011 (existence of the limit as the criterion) for the conceptual failure; BC-PRQ-01003 (evaluating each branch on its own side) for the procedural failure

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Determine whether the two sided limit exists at a discontinuity, and conclude that the discontinuity is removable only in that case.
skills.description_plain: Check whether the limit exists before claiming the break can be repaired.
skills.name: Decide whether a discontinuity can be removed

common_confusions: BC-MIS-01012 (unbounded behaviour assumed the same on both sides)
BC-MIS-01018 (infinite limit notation exchanged with limit at infinity notation)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-01009 (asymptote locations and one sided behaviour in correct notation carry separate credit)
adaptive.mastered_if: The statement records that f increases or decreases without bound as x approaches c, with the side carried on the arrow whenever the two sides behave differently, and the response does not write a single two sided infinite statement where the signs differ (BC-ERR-01019 absent) nor treat the statement as an existence claim for a real limit (BC-ERR-01020 absent).
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The unbounded behaviour is described correctly and the notation carries the wrong direction on one side, or the one sided markers are omitted although the two sides carry opposite signs, which is BC-ERR-01019.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The sign of the quotient on each side of the zero of the denominator cannot be determined, which is a gap at BC-PRQ-01009 and produces the same notation failure for a different reason.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-01012 (the infinity symbol as a description of behaviour, and its sign per side) for the conceptual failure; BC-SKL-01055 (the sign analysis that fixes each side) for the procedural failure

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Write the statement that f increases or decreases without bound as x approaches c, including the one sided form when the two sides behave differently.
skills.description_plain: Use the infinity symbol to record unbounded growth, with the side when it matters.
skills.name: Write an infinite limit using correct notation

common_confusions: BC-MIS-01011 (any zero of the original denominator read as unbounded behaviour)
BC-SKL-01041 (classifying the asymptotic case alone)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-01007 (both kinds of break appear in one function and must be classified separately with reasons)
adaptive.mastered_if: At a zero of the original denominator the response determines whether the factor divides out, and reports a removable discontinuity when it does and a vertical asymptote when it does not, with the factored form shown as the basis of the verdict (BC-ERR-01018 absent).
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The two cases are described correctly in general but the verdict for the given expression is taken from the unfactored denominator, so the distinction is stated and not applied.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: Neither numerator nor denominator can be factored, so the comparison that settles the case is unavailable, which is a gap at BC-PRQ-01001.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-01011 (what the surviving factor does that the cancelling one does not) for the conceptual failure; BC-PRQ-01001 (factoring both parts of the quotient) for the procedural failure

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a rational expression, determine whether a zero of the original denominator produces a removable discontinuity, because the factor divides out, or a vertical asymptote, because it does not.
skills.description_plain: Decide whether the factor cancels or survives.
